content: Hypophyseal hypertrophy during pregnancy refers to the physiological enlargement of the pituitary gland that occurs as a normal adaptation to pregnancy. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies have demonstrated that the pituitary gland increases in volume by approximately 30% during pregnancy. This enlargement typically results in an upward bulging of the gland. In most cases, the enlarged pituitary gland does not exert pressure on the optic chiasm, and therefore, visual field disturbances are rare. After delivery, the pituitary gland generally returns to its normal size. Despite the hyperplasia of the pituitary gland during pregnancy, there is no evidence to suggest an increased risk of developing pituitary tumors, such as prolactinomas.
